decision: Build src/core/bpmn-linter.ts (library) + src/cli/lint-bpmn.ts (CLI wrapper) with a custom, zero-dependency, fail-closed-whitelist XML tokenizer (src/core/bpmn-xml-parser.ts). The tokenizer's design invariant is: any byte sequence not unambiguously recognized as a known safe token class produces a parse-error token and the linter returns ok:false (whitelist, not blacklist). parseHandle is imported read-only from src/core/object-handle.ts (T-0015) as the single source of truth for handle validity. No new runtime npm dependencies. The deploy-gate contract (lintBpmn(xml):LintResult, reject on ok:false with HTTP 422) is frozen for T-0058/T-0064 in a deploy-contract stub doc.

rejected_alternatives.option: Use xmldom or fast-xml-parser as production runtime dependency
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates NF-1 (zero prod dep, Demiurge convention). Adds supply-chain audit surface to a security gate. The parser differential risk vs Flowable is reduced but not eliminated; the fail-closed-whitelist design is the correct mitigation regardless of parser choice.

rejected_alternatives.option: Use Node.js node:xml or WHATWG DOMParser
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Neither exists in Node >=20 built-ins. The spec acknowledges this.
Regex on raw XML is trivially bypassable via CDATA, attribute quoting, encoding tricks. The AC-8/AC-9 adversarial cases require tokenized extraction to avoid false-negatives. Rejected categorically.
Directly contradicts NF-4 and the orchestrator fail-closed-whitelist requirement. Skipping unknown constructs is the parser-differential exploit path. Rejected categorically.

rejected_alternatives.option: Scan raw XML bytes with string search instead of tokenizing
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Cannot reliably distinguish binding values from element names, comments, CDATA boundaries. The adversarial cases (attribute value in AC-8, CDATA in AC-9) require tokenized extraction.

rejected_alternatives.option: Use a maintained XML parser as dev-dependency inlined at build time
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Inlining third-party code into the production module is indistinguishable from a production dependency from an audit perspective, adds build complexity disproportionate to the problem size. The custom tokenizer is <300 lines and fully testable.
Out of scope per spec §8. Would require a maintained XML/XSD library (violates NF-1). The linter checks handle-discipline only.

contracts: export function lintBpmn(xml: string): LintResult  — pure, no I/O, no network, no DB; same input = same output
export interface LintViolation { type: LintViolationType; elementId: string; elementKind: string; message: string; }
export type LintResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; violations: LintViolation[] }
CLI: node dist/cli/lint-bpmn.js <file.bpmn>  — exit 0 on ok:true, exit 1 on ok:false; violations to stderr as JSON

Deploy-gate contract (T-0058/T-0064): (a) lintBpmn called before accepting deploy; (b) ok:false => HTTP 422 + violations; (c) malformed_xml => HTTP 422; (d) lintBpmn is pure, I/O is caller's; (e) T-0058 replaces mock deploy test with real endpoint
Import from T-0015 (read-only): import { parseHandle } from './object-handle.js' — single source of truth for handle validity; not re-exported

Raw-object detection pipeline: (1) if value starts with '{' attempt JSON.parse; (2) if result is object with record-identity or payload keys; (3) attempt parseHandle(v) — if succeeds, not a violation; if throws, violation
Fail-closed-whitelist: any XML construct not unambiguously recognized per §2.2 table => parse-error => ok:false
Namespace normalization: strip prefix up to ':' for local name matching; do not track namespace bindings

fitness_functions.rule: lintBpmn returns ok:true for handle-shaped and primitive bindings; ok:false for raw-object bindings in all scoped element types (serviceTask, userTask, sendTask, conditionExpression, dataObject, dataObjectReference)
fitness_functions.ci_check: vitest run src/__tests__/bpmn-linter.test.ts — AC-1..AC-10, AC-14, AC-15 green

fitness_functions.rule: Adversarial corpus: malformed XML (AC-6), raw object in attribute value (AC-8), raw object in CDATA (AC-9) all return ok:false
fitness_functions.ci_check: vitest run src/__tests__/bpmn-linter.test.ts — these three ACs must be green (adversarial subset)

fitness_functions.rule: LintViolation shape: all four fields present (type, elementId, elementKind, message); elementId is empty string when BPMN element has no id attribute
lintBpmn is a pure function: no process.exit, no fs.*, no http.*, no pg.*, no global state mutation in bpmn-linter.ts or bpmn-xml-parser.ts
fitness_functions.ci_check: tsc --noEmit (no I/O types leak into linter signature) + ci/checks/bpmn-linter-isolation.sh

fitness_functions.rule: bpmn-linter.ts and bpmn-xml-parser.ts import nothing from jobStore, http, pg, fs, net, or any package outside existing project devDependencies (NF-1 zero production deps)
fitness_functions.ci_check: ci/checks/bpmn-linter-isolation.sh — grep for forbidden imports in both files, exit 1 if found

fitness_functions.rule: No existing export of object-handle.ts, grant-resolver.ts, grant-lattice.ts, types.ts, or jobStore.ts is modified; git diff --name-only does not touch those files; existing test suites for those modules remain green (NF-3 / architect rule 7 / FE-W23-0008)
fitness_functions.ci_check: ci/checks/bpmn-linter-isolation.sh — git diff --name-only HEAD asserts no change to frozen modules; vitest run (all prior tests still pass)

fitness_functions.rule: CLI exits 0 on passing BPMN file, exits 1 on violations or malformed XML; violations are printed to stderr as valid JSON (NF-6)
fitness_functions.ci_check: vitest run src/__tests__/bpmn-linter.test.ts — AC-14 (integration fixture using node:child_process spawn)

fitness_functions.rule: Parser differential — all §2.2 reject conditions produce ok:false with type malformed_xml: DOCTYPE, non-predefined XML entities, duplicate attribute names, processing instructions, invalid UTF-8 bytes, XML 1.1 version declaration, null bytes, nesting depth >200
fitness_functions.ci_check: vitest run src/__tests__/bpmn-linter.test.ts — dedicated adversarial fixtures in src/__tests__/fixtures/bpmn-parser-adversarial/ covering each §2.2 row

fitness_functions.rule: No new entry in package.json dependencies section; only devDependencies allowed for test tooling
fitness_functions.ci_check: ci/checks/bpmn-linter-isolation.sh — node -e check that package.json dependencies does not contain any xml/bpmn/parser-related packages

§3.3 scoped elements (serviceTask) + §2.3 raw-object detector (registryId/recordId keys) + FF-1
§3.3 (conditionExpression) + §2.3 secondary embedded-object scan for EL script body (fields/payload keys) + FF-1
§3.1 tokenizer fail-closed (unclosed tags → parse-error token) + §2.2 reject table + FF-2, FF-8
§2.3 detection pipeline step 3: parseHandle(v) succeeds → not a violation; handle strings pass without false-positive + FF-1
§3.1 attribute value extraction (attrs[] on open-tag token) + §2.3 (raw object in attribute value) + FF-2 adversarial fixture
§3.1 CDATA → text token (CDATA content decoded and merged into text stream) + §2.3 + FF-2 adversarial fixture
§2.3 pipeline step 1: EL expression ${someVar} does not start with { in JSON sense or JSON.parse throws → no raw-object detected → ok:true + FF-1
§5.1 LintViolation interface (all 4 fields required, elementId='' when absent) + FF-3
§3 module boundary (linter imports only parseHandle from object-handle.ts and nothing else forbidden) + FF-5, FF-9
§5.3 compatibility surface (additive only, no modification to frozen exports) + FF-6
§3.4 CLI design (exit 0/1, violations to stderr as JSON) + FF-7
§3.5 deploy contract stub + §8 mock deploy fixture (mockDeploy calls lintBpmn, rejects on ok:false) + FF-1

runtime_target: local — npm run ci (tsc --noEmit && eslint src && npm run fitness && vitest run); no external resource. When T-0058 lands, lintBpmn runs as an in-process call in the Node.js API server before forwarding BPMN to Flowable deploy REST API. No new infra provisioned by T-0027.
